Great Stirrup Cay (port locode BSGSC) is part of Berry Islands (Bahamas). The small island (sized 270 acres / 0,4 mi2 / 1 km2) was purchased by Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings/NCLH in 1977 from Belcher Oil Company. Later, the property was developed into a private island used as a call port exclusively for NCLH-owned ships (from the fleets of NCL-Norwegian, Oceania and RSSC-Regent).

The nearest large island is Great Harbour Cay.

NCL private island Great Stirrup Cay (Bahamas)

In June 2016, NCL announced the company's plans to do an extensive makeover of its Bahamian private island. The project is part of "The Norwegian Edge" (USD 400 million fleet renovation program) and includes adding new attractions, eateries, private villas, zip-line course, underwater sculpture garden, new lagoon (suite-exclusive area), boardwalk (connecting the beach with the new entertainment complex).

Great Stirrup Cay's new landscaping works alone cost USD 1+ million. The private island destination was closed for refurbishment between August 25th and October 20th, 2016. However, due to damages caused by Hurricane Matthew, the opening was delayed until November 20th. The closure mostly affected the short itineraries of Norwegian Sky, which instead visited Nassau and Freeport (Grand Bahama) / Key West FL.

The new zip-line course (length 1000 ft / 305 m) has 2 parallel lines. The new underwater sculpture garden is a snorkeling/diving attraction (waterproof maps are provided). The half-mile (800 m) long boardwalk (connecting the beach with a new complex) is also a scenic walkway (100,000 ft2 / 9,290 m2) of new pathways. with shaded areas and rest stops with bench seating.

The half-acre-sized new entertainment complex has sports facilities (basketball-volleyball courts, tennis tables), a stage for live performances, shaded picnic area, air-conditioned reception center (board games rentals, reservations, locker rooms), complimentary food bar, new lounge area. Abaco Taco is a complimentary food bar near the new complex. LandShark Bar & Grill is another new (a la carte priced) eatery with indoor-outdoor seating.

All the island's existing eateries and bars were updated (decking, shaded areas, and stools in all bars). Dining venues' seating capacity was increased by 50%. The current buffet restaurant was redesigned and increased in seating capacity. In the ship tendering area were added new lockers and restrooms.

The new Lagoon Retreat is an adults-only private beach area with its own restaurant, covered area, air-conditioned private villas (1x 4-room Spa Villa, plus 22x villas/studios, 1-bedroom and 2-bedroom accommodations). The lagoon complex features a new swim-up bar, a family-dedicated shallow water beach, kids playground/picnic area, Silver Palm restaurant (complimentary, indoor-outdoor seating, rooftop terrace), private room (capacity 75 seats, used for private events / special occasions, with catering service).

Silver Cove is a 270-acres (23 km2) exclusive resort-style complex with a total of 38 beachfront villas, Mandara Spa (premium wellness facility), Moet Bar, Restaurant and Bar-Lounge.

  • Each Silver Cove Villa is fitted with power outlets, air-conditioner, HDTV with infotainment system (on-demand movies, Internet), full en-suite bathroom, daybeds, club chairs, retractable glass wall (for unobstructed beach views), spacious veranda (outdoor terrace with premium garden furniture). Other complimentary amenities and services provided to Silver Cove Villas include private beach access, buffet-style dining (at Silver Cove Restaurant). Six of the 1-Bedroom Villas are with wet bars and separate bedroom. 2-Bedroom Family Suite Villas additionally have separate indoor dining area, larger bedrooms and second bath (with whirlpool tub).
  • The types of villas available for rent are Studios (2-4 people), 1-Bedroom (4-6 people, with hot tub), 2-Bedroom (10 people, with hot tub, 2 bathrooms). All villas are with an open-air terrace, en-suite bathroom, living room (dining area). Food and drink services are also offered.
  • All villa rentals are price inclusive of air-conditioned shuttle transportation from the tender dock to Lagoon's reception.
  • The new Lagoon Retreat is an exclusive area for "The Haven" and all suite cruise passengers, and also for passengers with purchased on-land Mandara Spa treatments. A limited number of passes for all passengers are available for purchasing on each NCL Bahamas cruise with Great Stirrup Cay.

The island's renovations and upgrades were scheduled for completion by 2017 spring. The private cabanas were available for 2017 summer.  The beach getaway was spruced up with revamped and new food and drink venues, rebuilt cabanas, expanded sand beach areas, more lounge chairs (now 3000, up from 1200 prior to the refurbishment).

NCL's private island now offers a total of 38 private villas, a 2-story restaurant, a swim-up bar, a new spa area. The new landscaping resulted in over 1,000 trees, which expanded the island's shaded areas. Pathways were paved and additional seating was added around the outdoor venues.

Jumbey Beach Grill (the island's main buffet restaurant) was extensively refurbished and redesigned. Not it has 4 food lines (instead of 2), cutting down on crowds and speeding up service.  The buffet restaurant's upgrade alone cost around USD 0,75 million. The beach bars were enlarged. Jumby Beach received upgrades that resulted in food being cooked faster and staying fresher and hotter.

Other island improvements included Patron Bar and Bertram's Bar (new machines for frozen drinks and other equipment to speed up service). Bacardí Bar (serving mojito- and daiquiri cocktails) received more tables and umbrellas at its outdoor seating area, plus a live music band stand.

The above photo shows the island's adults-only area Lagoon Retreat.

In January 2025, NCLH started construction on Great Stirrup Cay's new pier (USD 150 million project) allowing the docking of two large ships simultaneously. In addition to the new pier, the project also included upgrades to the existing infrastructure.

In 2025, at Great Stirrup Cay were opened a new Welcome Center, an island-wide/expanded tram system, the Vibe Beach Club (an adults-only area with private cabanas, a bar, and exclusive access to a dedicated beachfront area), the Horizon Park (a recreational space with shaded relaxation areas and lawn games), and the Great Life Lagoon complex covering ~6000 m2/~64600 ft2. Great Life Lagoon consists of a large heated swimming pool (sized 2600 m2/28000 ft2, with a gradual, beach-style entry), two swim-up bars, a children's splash zone, and a surrounding sunbathing space/ring of private cabanas overlooking both the pool and the sea waters.

The new Splash Harbor is a separate (complimentary) water playground for kids.

Great Tides Waterpark

On July 29, 2025, NCL announced plans for Great Stirrup Cay to have a large waterpark, scheduled for inauguration on September 4, 2026, with the arrival of Norwegian Luna.

Great Tides Waterpark's day passes were opened for purchace on May 28th (2026).

Following the completion of this major infrastructure development project (representing ~USD 150 million investment by NCLH), the expansion increased the annual visits to the island to 1+ million tourists (across 15 ships) in 2026, marking a significant growth from 2024's ~400,000.

The Great Tides Waterpark occupies an area of ~6 acres (~24300 m2). Its most popular facilities and amenities include the Wandering River (a 800-ft/244-m-long lazy river), the Tidal Tower (height 170 ft/52 m, with 8 slides), 19 total waterslides (racing, tube, spins, some slides have conveyor belts lifting the rafts to the Tidal Tower's top), a splash zone for kids (Tidepool Town, size 9000 ft2/836 m2, with a large tipping bucket positioned 40 ft/12 m above the ground), The Grotto Bar (beneath The Great Slide at Cliffside Cove), Floataway Bar (within the Wandering River), cliffside jumps, a mini racecourse with jet karts.

The Cliffside Cove has racer slides, 2 cliff jumping platforms (10 ft and 15 ft tall), and a family slide.

The Wandering River's highlights include an illuminated tunnel (fitted with a bioluminescent scene), cabanas, and a splash zone.

Other new facilities introduced at Great Stirrup Cay include a double ship pier, a welcome plaza, complimentary tram service (throughout the entire island), the Great Life Lagoon (1,4 acre, with a large heated swimming pool, rental cabanas and villas, complimentary premium loungers, 2 swim-up bars - named Reef Bar, and The Waves Bar), the Splash Town (sized 3400 ft2/316 m2, with interactive water fountains, a shaded bar lounge), the Horizon Park (designed for recreational activities - lawn games, pickleball courts, a 9-hole mini golf course, half sports court), the Hammock Bay (50+ hammocks, and a bar near the BBQ Buffet), and the adults-only Vibe Shore Club (a bar, hanging daybeds, premium lounge seating).

Dining venues include Low Tide Smoke (serving slow-smoked barbecue food, including St. Louis-style pork riblets, pork nachos, chicken wings, and Buffalo cauliflower), Catch of the Day (seafood bar offering crispy shrimp rolls, fried shrimp baskets, chilled seafood rolls), Tidal Treats (desserts bar offering bubble-waffle sundaes, fish-shaped waffle cones with soft-serve ice cream and a selection of flavoured toppings). Complimentary buffet dining is also be available within the waterpark.

Great Stirrup Cay cruise terminal

Below you can see the island's map showing its best attractions and amenities.

The island's northern part features snorkeling areas and a sandy beach surrounded by rocky outcroppings.

The island's southern part has a helicopter field (signed "Great Stirrup Cay International Airport") as part of a former US military installation for satellite tracking.

There is an original lighthouse (constructed in 1863).

The most common tree is the coconut palm, which milk and meat is used in most of the drink recipes.

As wildlife, the island has different varieties of lizards and land crabs, seagulls and sanderlings (waders / shorebirds).

The climate is tropical. Average temperatures are 75 F / 24 C (December-April) and 85–93 F / 29–34 C (May-November). Average sea water temperatures are 81–86 F / 27–30 C (May-November) and 77 F / 25 C (December-April).
